alex_customer: Hey team — our dedicated pool (eu-west-2, pool-id: dp-88) started seeing p95 jumps from ~120ms -> 1.2s and intermittent 429s for inference requests since ~09:40 UTC. Only affects tenant acme-x. No config changes on our side. Any obvious noisy neighbor checks to run?

elaine_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Alex. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces? Also which model and MIG profile are you using?

alex_customer: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-13b-ocq","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}'
Model: rw-13b-ocq, allocated as MIG partition mpc-2g. We see the p95 jump every ~30s for bursts, looks like short spikes.

omar_sre: I'm seeing correlated SM bursts on host h-eu2-42 around the same times. Runs show sibling MIG slice (id: mig-0b4) hitting ~95% SM for 2-3s, then drops. Appears periodically across tenants on that host. Posting quick snapshot from agent: 

sre-bot: ```
[2026-03-17T09:45:02Z] host=h-eu2-42
GPU0: A100-SXM4
 MIG-slice-001 (tenant=acme-x): SM 18% mem 2.1G
 MIG-slice-002 (tenant=other-1): SM 96% mem 7.9G <-- bursting
 MIG-slice-003 (tenant=infra-bench): SM 12% mem 0.3G
 dstat: net 0.1ms, io 0.0ms
 kernel throttling: none
```

mike_infra: Thanks, Omar. Two quick hypotheses: 1) fractional packing + autoscaler burst placed a high-SM workload on a sibling slice and we didn't respect tenant affinity when filling idle slices; 2) KV-cache lockstep warmup causing short SM saturation when a heavy request hits one slice.

jess_engineer: To reproduce quickly: run our loadgen pinned to that pool with 8 concurrent clients and 1k small prompts (sequence length 64) and watch p95. Command: 
```bash
loadgen --pool dp-88 --concurrency 8 --requests 1000 --model rw-13b-ocq --seq 64
```
If you see the periodic spike, collect `nvprof`/`nsys` or at least `gpustat` snapshots.

omar_sre: Ran jess's loadgen for 15m. Repro'd the ~30s spikes. Profiling shows kernel launch bursts on MIG slice 002. Memory bandwidth stays steady; it's SM launch saturation. Looks like a sibling tenant doing short heavy matrix ops.

elaine_support: For immediate mitigation: 1) move acme-x off h-eu2-42 to another host (manual drain) or 2) change autoscale policy to stop bursting into partially-filled hosts. Which do you prefer, Alex?

alex_customer: Prefer a quick move if possible, we need p95 back to normal. Also happy to test scheduler changes later.

mike_infra: I'm going to initiate a live migrate for acme-x to a different host in the same pool and pin a placement constraint for 24h. Doing `redwoodctl admin migrate-tenant --tenant acme-x --target-host h-eu2-11 --pin 24h` now.

sre-bot: ```
[action] migrate started: tenant=acme-x -> h-eu2-11
[progress] draining 2 active workers (expected 45s)
[done] migrate complete at 09:51:05Z
```

jess_engineer: After migrate, re-ran loadgen for 10m. No periodic spikes observed, p95 back to ~130ms. :thumbsup:

elainE_support: (typo) meant to say great — we'll keep this pinned and open a follow-up ticket for the scheduler to prefer "empty-slice-first" allocation to avoid colocating heavy short-burst workloads with latency-sensitive tenants.

omar_sre: For postmortem notes: collect the offending tenant's job traces (other-1) for burst pattern, add a rule to avoid placing critical slices next to bursty tenants for 72h until longer-term scheduler change. Also add a KV-cache warmup guard: small warmup QPS cap per slice to avoid lockstep.

alex_customer: Thanks all. Please cc me on the follow-up ticket. Appreciate the fast triage. :eyes:

elaine_support: Will do — created ticket INF-4572 and added acme-x as impacted. Assigning to @mike_infra and @omar_sre for scheduler follow-up. Action items: [migrate done], [pin acme-x 24h], [collect other-1 traces], [scheduler ticket INF-4572].

mike_infra: noted. I'll also add a temporary autoscale policy tweak for dp-88 to prefer new hosts for 48h.

sre-bot: Reaction added :white_check_mark: to migrate step.
